chunks: And it is narrated from Bakr ibn Muhammad that he said:

I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and with me was ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz. He said to me, "Who is this?" I said, "Our mawlā." He said, "Did you free him or his father?" I said, "Rather, his father." He said, "This is not your mawlā; this is your brother and your cousin. The mawlā is only the one upon whom the blessing has directly been bestowed; so if it was bestowed upon his father, then he is your brother and your cousin."

He said: A man asked him while I was present, saying: "I have a غلام who drinks and becomes involved in these disliked matters, and I wish to free him. Is it more beloved to you that I free him, or that I sell him and give his price in charity?" He said, "Indeed, manumission is more virtuous at some times, and at other times charity is more virtuous. Manumission is more virtuous when the people are in a good condition, but when the people are in hardship, then charity is more virtuous. And selling this one is more beloved to me when he is in this state."

key_terms.أَعْتَقْتُمُوهُ: you freed him; granted manumission directly
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ: charity given for the sake of Allah
key_terms.الْغُلَامُ: the slave or young male servant being discussed
key_terms.بِثَمَنِهِ: for his price; the sale value given away
key_terms.مَوْلَاكَ: your mawlā; the one directly linked through manumission

ai.seo_question: When is freeing a slave better than selling him and giving the money in charity according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the legal and social usage of mawlā, distinguishing between the one directly emancipated and his descendants, who are treated instead as kin. It also gives a contextual ruling on whether freeing a slave or selling him and giving his price as charity is preferable, depending on public circumstances and the moral condition of the slave.
